evidence: Parsed every task judge.toml with tomllib. Gates: hro_gate_render and hro_gate_shared are type=binary (gates must stay binary per staged-task-contract.md:96); both are reachability/real-backend pass-fail checks. Functional: all 43 criteria type=binary (weights 0.5-2.5); each is a discrete product rule with explicit 'Fails if ...' conditions and positive controls (e.g. hro_interview_full, hro_stale_refused, hro_thread_latest 'most recent 30 messages'). A grep for degree wording (well|polished|quality|clear|good|appropriate|reasonable) in functional, gate and polish criteria returned no matches, so no craft judgement is flattened into binary. Polish: 5 criteria, all binary (hro_pol_live_board, _live_thread, _earlier_place, _failed_send, _session_resume). These are conjunctive behavioural preservation checks (draft text/focus/scroll survive a live update, getBoundingClientRect position within a few pixels, failed send explained and not lost/duplicated, session-end prompt and per-user drafts), not degree-of-quality judgements; binary fits and matches the template's binary polish dimension. Visual: 5 criteria (hro_vis_type, _color, _layout, _hierarchy, _consistency), all type=likert, points=5, weight 1.2, each with a described anchor at every level 5,4,3,2,1 (scored/visual/judge.toml:23-90). Craft/degree-of-quality is therefore likert with anchors, as #41 requires. Scale consistency: the task uses raw 1-5 anchors while the template prompt advertises a 0-5 scale. Pinned harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7 (tests/Dockerfile:31) Likert(points=5) requests raw 1-5 and normalizes (raw-1)/4 (NEW_TASK_AUTHORING_CONTEXT.md:239; brickfall check.py:11 asserts [0,.25,.5,.75,1]). The task's visual prompt.md:7,12,16 consistently says the minimum is 'raw Likert 1, which normalizes to zero' for failed gate, nonworking features, and NOT EXERCISED. So every in-schema level has an anchor; the template's 0 anchor would be outside RewardKit's requested range. Polish/functional/gate prompts consistently say 'binary 0; Likert 1'. Workbook internal annotation ('Likert we dont use in rewrdkit') is the known false positive in SKILL.md; judged against the shipped format per the skill. Adversarial checks: (a) Broken app that could pass: a functionally weak but attractive app cannot use this row's type choice to gain points; visual likert mass (0.2) is behind the gates and functional floor 0.05 in scoring.toml/score.py:41-48, which belong to rows 42/43. (b) Conforming alternative that could fail: no binary row requires a stylistic choice. The visual prompt says 'Layout, labels and styles are the implementer's choice' and 'Do not deduct the same observed defect in more than one row', so an unconventional but coherent design is graded on gradient anchors, not pass/fail. No counterexample found for this row. Limitation: there is no configured judge run (raw-evidence-index scope says full configured grading is absent), so actual judge use of the anchors is not exercised. This is a static schema/fit row, so that does not leave a defect open here.
